moa.description: The measured active B12 provides an established methionine-synthase cofactor precursor; uptake and intracellular cofactor conversion were not directly traced.
moa.evidenceQualification: Food-supply connection supported; mediation of the homocysteine change was not isolated.

semanticReview.rationale: Summary is limited to measured food provision of B12, not demonstrated intracellular conversion or causal mediation of homocysteine. Existing description and qualifications retained.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: At 5 g/day, serum B12 and holoTC rose, homocysteine fell, and the combined B12-status index improved versus control after baseline adjustment.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Upstream B12 supply; not direct methionine-synthase flux.

evidenceSource.population: 30 vegetarians, 20–50 years, without recent B12 supplements
evidenceSource.exposure: 5 or 8 g/day tested unflavoured roasted nori for four weeks; actual trial-batch B12 approximately 1.9/3.1 µg/day

limitations.text: Between-group MMA and folate changes were not significant; no significant advantage of 8 over 5 g.
Product B12 varies; not all seaweed is equivalent.
Did not eliminate deficiency in all participants; no replacement for established deficiency treatment.
Small, short, unblinded study; no tissue flux or clinical benefit measured.

adjudication.eligibility: Evidence supports a bounded dietary protocol through the admitted B12 supply relationship.
adjudication.implementation_status: Implemented; MDX, protected fields, presentation, governance and browser six-atom checks passed; final production rebuild pending
adjudication.material: Studied roasted purple-laver product; no new quantitative composition edge
